rationale: fastdiff_flow_pixel_unconstrained-claude-agentic: image_size=512, pixel_spacing=0.3516, n_angles=128, n_det=1024, det_spacing=0.35754, sod=500.0, sdd=1000.0, display_min=0.0, display_max=0.5, train_n=400, val_n=200, noise_i0=100000.0, noise_sigma_e=10.0, seed=42, fd_recon_ckpt=/cluster/maier/Agent4CT/checkpoints/fast_diffusion_pixel_breast.pt, fd_recon_steps=8, fd_recon_init=fbp, fd_recon_init_t=0.2, fd_recon_eta=1.0, fd_recon_dc=0, fd_recon_dc_n_cg=5, fd_recon_dc_relax=0.5, rationale=iter-3: DC-off breast-prior. ONE KNOB init_t 0.4->0.2. TREND: iter-1 (init_t0.7) PSNR19.0/RMSE3.8e-2; iter-2 (init_t0.4) PSNR24.6/RMSE2.0e-2 - monotonic fidelity gain as init_t drops (less injected noise, sampler stays nearer the measured FBP). Both hr=0 (sparse-FBP baseline PSNR36.3/RMSE5.2e-3 is a very strong bar for a DC-free prior sampler). HYPOTHESIS: init_t=0.2 pushes PSNR further toward the FBP baseline because the DC-free sampler reduces to a light prior-denoise of the FBP init; tests whether the breast prior ALONE can approach (not just trail) the baseline. If PSNR keeps rising monotonically, the prior contributes fidelity only insofar as it preserves the FBP - the DC step (absent here) is what would let it EXCEED baseline.
